slides.title: AI News Building Better Through Constraints David Heinemeier
slides.text: AI News Building Better Through Constraints David Heinemeier Hansson, 37signals co-owner and Basecamp creator, in a long-form interview He argues that software improves when teams deliberately limit features, resources, and interruptions The discussion covers Basecamp’s 2004 launch, current AI-assisted development, and his work on the Omarchy Linux distribution Problem: abundant resources and large teams can encourage bloated products, forced upgrades, and needless complexity Solution: Preserve constraints, keep proven software stable, build for real jobs , and favor focused small teams Achievement: Basecamp was initially built in 380 hours and still supports profitable legacy versions for longtime customers Key lesson: Use AI to sharpen judgment - not merely to produce more code. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=76rR68ktQvo https://basecamp.com https://37signals.com https://omarchy.us

slides.title: AI News AI Agents Build a Complex App
slides.text: AI News AI Agents Build a Complex App Feature The creator of Enjoy, an AI-agent app, describes using Claude Opus 5.5 in Ultra Code to implement a 2,700-line specification for team collaboration. The project involved redesigning the app for multiple users and coordinating phones, browsers, desktop clients, a relay server, and encrypted traffic. The creator says the agent worked for about seven hours, using dozens of implementation and review agents, with tests and CI checks. He reports that the feature matched the specification and worked well, contrasting it with earlier agents that failed on smaller tasks and left codebases broken. His proposed shift is from manually reviewing every line to evolutionary coding : automated tests, adversarial agent reviews, and production results guide iteration . The achievement suggests AI may shorten complex development and change engineering practice. https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/overview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2zLuYU_Ub_0

slides.text: Claude Code Mods Claude Code Mods Mods = JavaScript handlers that customize Claude Code assistant Claude Code Mods are small add-ons that change Claude Code’s interface or behavior mods require version 2.1.287 or newer To create a mod, just describe the feature you want - and Claude builds the mod Enable hot reloading to try it immediately in the terminal or desktop Code tab To keep it, ask Claude to save and install it as a plugin so it remains available in future sessions Examples: a tool counter, destructive-command guard, prompt simplifier, context-usage meter. slides.title: AI News Kent Beck on Craft and AI-Assisted
slides.text: AI News Kent Beck on Craft and AI-Assisted Development Kent Beck is known for his book Extreme Programming (XP, 1999) - Agile approach to building software - deliver small improvements often, get feedback quickly, and adapt rather than trying to plan everything up front https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_Programming https://extremeprogrammingalliance.com/about-extreme-programming-xp/ Common XP practices include: Test-driven development (TDD), Pair programming, Continuous integration, Small releases and regular customer feedback, Refactoring: improve the code’s structure https://www.agile-academy.com/en/agile-dictionary/extreme-programming/ Kent Beck warns that AI-generated code may be broken; developers must verify behavior rather than trust appearances His solution: work iteratively, test continuously, and alternate shipping features with refactoring that preserves future choices This balance enables learning and keeps software adaptable, instead of rapidly accumulating complexity until change becomes dangerous Beck argues that code volume do not prove progress https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aSXaxOdVtAQ https://kentbeck.com https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/how-kent-beck-shapes-the-software

slides.title: AI News Manus 2.0 and Cue Agent app
slides.text: AI News Manus 2.0 and Cue Agent app - web, desktop, and mobile Manus’s Cascade harness, Studio, and cloud computers let agents handle projects, edit videos, build games, run automations, and work remotely Cue gives each agent an email, phone number, wallet, and computer https://manus.im/blog/introducing-manus-2-0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L75zF2WKiVE Research - AI Improves Its Own Design Weco AI is based in London, UK Weco’s AIDE² experiment - "autoresearch on autoresearch" Used two nested AI-agent loops . The inner agent tried to improve solutions to research and engineering tasks; the outer agent repeatedly rewrote the inner agent’s harness code , evaluated the rewrite under a fixed cost budget, and kept it only if it improved on a hidden score The system changed the agent’s scaffolding, not the underlying model weights Over eight days, the system ran 100 rounds, proposing and testing changes; seven upgrades survived hidden evaluations Its best version, AIDE85, outperformed Weco’s two-year, hand-tuned baseline on held-out benchmarks under a fixed budget. The result offers public evidence for level-one recursive self-improvement: an AI system improving faster than manual tuning https://www.weco.ai/blog/first-evidence-of-recursive-self-improvement https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26457 https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/

slides.title: AI News HumanLayer - The Multiplayer Coding Agent
slides.text: AI News HumanLayer - The Multiplayer Coding Agent Workspace TL;DR - AI agents can implement features quickly, but humans must retain product, architectural, and program-design control Problem: Coding factories can create unreviewed, poorly structured code, leaving teams unable to diagnose serious bugs months later Solution: Define measurable user outcomes, architecture, interfaces, tests, and small end-to-end vertical slices before agents generate large changes The approach shifts engineers toward high-leverage design, verification, and prioritization Note: Benchmarks that merely pass tests do not measure maintainability; sustained human understanding and feedback remain essential https://humanlayer.com https://x.com/dexhorthy

slides.title: AI News Agentic AI Token Use is Much
slides.text: AI News Agentic AI Token Use is Much Bigger that Human Human tokens are input and output text tokens from direct, human-driven AI interactions. For example, a person submitting a document and receiving its summary. Prompt, document, and summary - all count towards "human" tokens Agentic tokens come from automated AI workflows that make repeated model calls, use tools, retain context, and execute multi-step tasks such as coding, research, or debugging. OpenRouter classifies traffic from behavioral signals including tool calls, number of conversation turns, and request timing - not simply whether a human initiated the work. Agentic usage overtook human usage on Feb 6, 2026. By August 10, agentic traffic reached 7.3 trillion tokens on a seven-day average, versus 1.4 trillion human-driven tokens: over 5× larger. From February, agents grew about 14×; human usage grew 2.8×. https://cryptobriefing.com/openrouter-agentic-token-usage-14x-growth/

slides.text: AI News OpenAI publishes 722 math papers from an unreleased model 722 manuscripts in 372 result families, posted on GitHub Model tried about 4,000 open research problems Boldest claim: a proof of a quasi-Riemann hypothesis 162 papers have their main results checked in Lean Average cost: about 3 hours of ChatGPT Pro compute per result Levent Alpöge (Anthropic): "the most significant moment in mathematical history" Nothing is peer reviewed yet; some mathematicians are angry about the volume https://github.com/openai/math Cloudflare Integrates Pi Durable Cloudflare and Earendil integrated Pi Durable into Cloudflare’s Agents SDK. The new PiHarness class runs Pi-powered agents inside Cloudflare Durable Objects, connecting the agent harness to persistent SQLite storage. Long-running agents can lose progress when interrupted. Persisted state and lifecycle alarms let interrupted runs resume after eviction. The integration combines agent execution, persistence, and recovery, making resilient agents easier to deploy. PiHarness is beta; Pi Durable is experimental, so APIs may change. https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/pi/

slides.text: Tech Hiring Software job postings on Indeed Comparing to 2020 level, in Feb 2022 it was 234%, in 2025 it was 65%, now it is 77% All US job postings: 103% (compared with 2020) Postings that mention AI: 6.7% of all, up from 3.4% a year ago https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IHLIDXUSTPSOFTDEVE Skills in demand Dice, 7M+ US tech postings (Aug 2026): +18% year over year AI and machine learning postings +101% year over year, five times the overall rate Fastest-growing skills, each up 200%+: responsible AI, AI agents, agentic AI, AI infrastructure Most requested overall: communication, computer science, troubleshooting Indeed: 71% of the software postings rebound (May 2025 to May 2026) is senior roles; 37% has AI in the title https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/ https://www.dice.com/hiring/recruitment/reports/dice-tech-job-report Top "In Demand" Skills and Qualifications - Critical thinking and problem-solving - Communication and stakeholder management - Adaptability and continuous learning - AI literacy and practical AI adoption - AI/ML application development - Data engineering and data management - Cybersecurity and risk management - Cloud and infrastructure engineering - Software engineering - Automation and workflow optimization - DevOps, CI/CD, and platform engineering - Governance, compliance, and responsible AI - Analytical thinking and data analysis - Product management and business alignment - Project and program management - Leadership and cross-functional collaboration - Creativity and innovation - Resilience and professionalism - Technical troubleshooting and systems thinking - Business growth and customer focus
